name: uniques-census

variantDescriptions.census: `claude/uniques-audit` `9d4de2f228`: retronym/scala#212 + retronym/scala#239 (squashed) + the census probe. Counters in `audit-<pid>.json`, read with `perflab api audit`

description: Audit, not a timing: what becomes of each type the `uniques` table interns, to judge which types could be held strongly (no `WeakReference`) and which need not be interned at all. Each type is tagged at intern time with its class, phase, whether it was made inside a completion ([retronym/scala#212](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/212)'s `CompletionFrame`) and whether it refers to a method's params (as in retronym/scala3#112) or to skolems/existentials. Its fate is one of: `anchoredSame` (reachable from a symbol's info or type cache, set in the same frame entry that made it: a mark at construction could catch it), `anchoredLater`, `anchoredCleared` (anchored through a symbol that then died, so anchoring at that `setInfo` would have leaked it), `clearedFree`, `liveFree` (never anchored, alive at the end of the run).

Counters are over the whole fork (all runs, warmup included); `perflab api audit` divides by ops. Local pilot on scalap (one run, 41K types): anchoredSame 25%, anchoredCleared 25% (mostly via type caches and params of cloned symbols), clearedFree 31%, liveFree 19%; 36% of types refer to a method's params.
